## Zoning & Development Analysis — 1218 W George St, Chicago IL
**PIN: 14291230290000** | Parcel resolution: authoritative | Code current through Council Journal of March 18, 2026

---

### 1. Zoning District Currently in Effect

This parcel is zoned **RT-4 (Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse & Multi-Unit)** [§17-2-0103]. This is confirmed via the City's official GIS parcel record — you can verify it on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Is Residential Use Allowed?

**Yes, emphatically.** RT-4 is a residential district whose permitted uses include detached houses, two-flats, townhouses, multi-unit buildings (3+ units), parks, schools, religious institutions, and home occupations [§17-2-0103]. Residential use is the primary, by-right use of this district.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

From the zoning table for RT-4 [§17-2-0103] and the density rules at [2]:

| Standard | Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 1.2 |
| **Max Height** | 38 ft |
| **Min Lot Area per Dwelling Unit** | 1,000 sq ft |
| **Min Lot Size** | 1,650 sq ft |

**Unit yield (lot area only):** The parcel is 3,075 sq ft. At 1,000 sq ft per unit: 3,075 ÷ 1,000 = **3 units by lot area** [2]. *Important caveat: lot area per unit is a floor constraint only — FAR, height, parking, and unit-size requirements can further limit what's buildable, while ground-floor Type A accessible units are exempt from the per-unit count* [2].

**Setbacks:** No side-setback figure is specified in the retrieved code text for RT-4 specifically (side-setback detail appears in [4] for B/C districts, not RT). Front and rear setback minimums were not in the retrieved text — contact the Department of Buildings or the Zoning Help Desk (312-744-5000) to confirm.

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

Three overlays apply. No others.

- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — The parcel is in a CTA TOD overlay, reflecting its proximity to the Wellington Brown/Purple Line station (0.34 miles). See parking discussion in §5.
- **ADU Eligible Area** — Additional Dwelling Units (conversion units and/or coach houses) may be permitted on this parcel under [1]. Coach houses in RS-designated lots require compliance with [3]; since this parcel is RT-4, coach-house rules at [3] also apply. The ADU program is enforced by the Department of Housing [1].
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** [5] — Any qualifying residential development triggering ARO thresholds must provide affordable units or pay an in-lieu fee. The Lake View community area has 20 ARO-related affordable housing projects totaling 432 units already in place, including developments like Optima Lakeview (3460 N. Broadway, 11 units) and Low-Line Commons (3421 N. Ashland, 5 units).

**Not applicable:** No Planned Development, no landmark or historic district designation, no Special Service Area, no lakefront protection, no Special District, no PMD, no flood hazard (FEMA Zone X — minimal flood hazard).

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit-Related Reduction

Because this parcel is in a CTA TOD area, the minimum off-street parking requirement **may be reduced by up to 100%** under §17-10-0102-B — meaning parking could potentially be eliminated entirely for a qualifying development. [data:permits] Required parking spaces for residential uses must generally be located on the same zoning lot [4]. Note that **no density, FAR, or height bonus applies** in RT-4: those bonuses are available only in "dash-3" districts (e.g., B1-3, B2-3, C1-3, etc.) under §17-3-0402-B, §17-3-0403-B, and §17-3-0408-B — RT-4 is not among them.

---

### 6. Has the Zoning Changed Recently?

**Yes — this parcel was recently rezoned.** The current RT-4 designation was established by **ordinance O2026-0025358**, dated **June 16, 2026**, with the zoning map updated **August 21, 2026**. You can view the ordinance record directly at the [City Clerk's ELMS portal](https://chicityclerkelms.chicago.gov/Matter/?matterId=39EAE819-E452-F111-BEC6-001DD80B0E39). The RT-4 standards described above are the **currently applicable standards**. Note that zoning map amendments can take up to 90 days to fully propagate, and a later Municipal Code amendment may not yet be reflected in the code text (current through March 18, 2026).

---

### Confidence & Limitations

**High confidence on:** District classification (authoritative PIN match), permitted uses, FAR/height/density figures (from the zoning table, not recalled from memory), overlay applicability, the recent rezoning, and parking reduction eligibility.

**Could not determine:** Specific front/rear/side setback dimensions for RT-4 (not in retrieved code text); assessed value (no assessment history on record); comparable sales (none returned). For setbacks, consult the full RT-4 standards at §17-2-0400 or the Zoning Help Desk.
